result:
**Verdict: PASS** for DG1 round 4, domain-reviewer (T-DG1-REV-DOM-R4), on candidate `sha256:3b76021be348356f…08fb1` (source commit `016433d`). I recomputed the candidate ID and it matched. HEAD is the freeze commit `e8ed6e2`, which only adds the round-4 assignments, the manifest and `stages.json`. The clone is complete, not shallow.

**Findings I verified (both now CLOSED_VERIFIED)**
- **F-DG1-009 (Medium, integration determinism): fixed.** I ran the full integration suite 9 times, each on a fresh throwaway PostgreSQL 16.13. All 9 passed 200/200 with exit 0.
  - Test files now run one at a time; the run logs show no overlap between files.
  - There was no unhandled 57P01 error and no scratch database was left behind.
  - The check that "a denied create writes nothing" passed 14/14 in every run.
  - The new scratch-drop test passed 3/3 in every run.
  - One open point: in run 5 the database server logged a single FATAL line that the test client never saw. My script counted it but didn't print it, and the log was deleted with the cluster, so I couldn't identify it. Four more runs with full server logging showed none. I've noted it in the verification; it isn't a finding.
- **F-DG1-210 (Medium, UX): fixed.** I tested it live in Arabic (RTL) and English (LTR). A Lead whose role covers only one business unit created a record through the form. Edit, Archive and the audit trail appeared about 140 ms later without a page reload, and the app re-read `/api/v1/me` once. The derived grant already showed, translated, in the audit trail. The Edit button works for real: the rename was saved by the server at version 2 and wrote one audit event. The 4 new unit tests pass, including "no extra access granted" and "a failed refresh never blocks".

**Round-3 closures still hold**
- **F-DG1-001:** closing a transformation is still refused with 422 and the G6 message. Nothing was written, and the edit form offers no "closed" option.
- **F-DG1-002 and F-DG1-105:** all 11 modules are present, including the workflows, kpi and reporting scaffolds, each with its own tests.
- **F-DG1-003:** the glossary tests pass 8/8, and the Arabic text has no glossary-term conflation.
- **F-DG1-004, F-DG1-005 and F-DG1-008:** the record's creator and a second user both see a translated audit trail. Names are shown, never raw IDs, and untranslated entries are clearly marked.
- **F-DG1-006 and F-DG1-207:** the API spec lints clean with 33 operations, and the contract tests pass 9/9.
- **F-DG1-007:** the requirements register is unchanged since round 3.

**Invariants and requirements**
- **Invariants hold:**
  - Branding is still marked provisional. The branding API returns provisional values and refuses unauthenticated calls with 401, and all 34 colour tokens are flagged provisional.
  - There is no claim of official Mobily or PMI status.
  - Arabic renders RTL and English LTR. No request goes outside the app (no CDN), and the fonts are bundled.
  - No floating-point money types exist, and missing data shows as Unknown.
  - Product gates G1–G6 stay separate from DG0–DG7.
- **Requirements:** all 12 rows due at DG1 are IMPLEMENTED, and every evidence file they cite exists. The other assigned rows (REQ-S16-023, PB-001, PB-003, PB-009, S03-003, S15-007, S15-008, S15-011) are honestly marked SPECIFIED with later gates.

**New findings:** none.

`08-static-checks.out.txt` includes an error from one of my own probes (a wrong token path). I re-ran that probe correctly and recorded the result in `09-register-modules.out.txt`, which the record notes.

The review record passes its schema check, and all 81 evidence references exist as files. I deleted the disposable clone afterwards.

Files are in `docs/delivery/`:
- `reviews/DG1/round-4/domain-reviewer.json`
- `reviews/DG1/round-4/domain-reviewer.verifications.json`
- `test-evidence/DG1/domain/round-4/` (scripts, run logs, and 12 Arabic/English screenshots)
